questions.stem: How do Data Discrepancies relate to Data Errors?
options: They are the same thing
Data Errors are searched for, identified and fixed based on Data Discrepancies
Data Discrepancies are caused only by Data Errors
Data Errors are a type of Data Discrepancy
Neither can occur without a data warehouse
questions.explanation: Data Discrepancies are often confused with Data Errors, but a discrepancy is the signal: data errors are then searched for, identified and fixed based on it.

questions.stem: What is the dictionary definition of a discrepancy?
options: An exact match between two facts
An illogical or surprising lack of compatibility or similarity between two or more facts
A record that has been deleted
A summary of detailed data
A change in the data arriving at a model
questions.explanation: A discrepancy is an illogical or surprising lack of compatibility or similarity between two or more facts.

questions.stem: Which situation is described as a Data Discrepancy?
options: A dashboard loading in under three seconds
A model retrained after new product types appear
Manual calculations by a data analyst not matching numbers from automated reports
A dataset shared with the QA team
A query with no WHERE clause
questions.explanation: When an analyst's manual calculations do not match the automated report, there is a data reconciliation issue, which is a Data Discrepancy.

questions.stem: In the *I Am Datapedia!* example, why do 9,093 plus 6,104 not equal the 'All Users' total of 14,018?
options: Because the totals came from different sources
Because the arithmetic was done wrongly
Because one figure was encrypted
Because the report was in MDX
Because the data was synthetic
questions.explanation: The 14,018 total came from various sources while 9,093 and 6,104 came from different sources, so the figures do not reconcile: a Data Discrepancy.

questions.stem: Once Data Discrepancies are found, what is the next step?
options: Delete the conflicting reports
Migrate the data to the cloud
Retrain the machine learning model
Start identifying data errors, code errors and business rule errors
Add more filters to the dashboard
questions.explanation: After discrepancies are found, the next step is to identify the underlying data, code or business rule errors.

questions.stem: Does a Data Discrepancy always mean there is a data issue?
options: Yes, always
No, discrepancies never indicate data issues
No, discrepancies are always caused by hardware faults
Yes, unless the data is in the cloud
No, it may be that not all facts were used when processing both sides of the data
questions.explanation: It is not always a data issue; sometimes the two sides were produced using different facts, such as one analyst filtering out a region.

questions.stem: In the two-analyst example, why do the two reports' totals not match?
options: One summed all rows while the other filtered out one of the regions
One analyst used SQL and the other used MDX
One report was run in development
The table had duplicate primary keys
The second analyst used synthetic data
questions.explanation: The first analyst summed all rows; the second reported sales by region but filtered one region out, so the totals differ without any data error.

questions.stem: Where are Data Discrepancies normally found?
options: In synthetic datasets
In OLAP cubes
In data sitting in silos
In geocoded records
In canned reports
questions.explanation: Data Discrepancies are normally found when data is sitting in silos, which is why the Single Source of Truth concept surfaced.

questions.stem: Which concept surfaced to address Data Discrepancies caused by silos?
options: Data Island
Scope Creep
Concept Drift
Single Source of Truth, delivered by a Data Warehouse
Canned Data
questions.explanation: The Single Source of Truth concept arose so that a Data Warehouse could bring all data silos together in one place.

questions.stem: In which data model forms does a Data Warehouse ideally consolidate silos to avoid Data Discrepancies?
options: Multiple isolated data islands
Separate development instances per team
A landing zone only
A collection of spreadsheets
One Unified Data Model, or a Star or Snowflake schema
questions.explanation: A Data Warehouse brings silos together ideally in one Unified Data Model or in Star or Snowflake schemas.
